claims.text: A machine-learning approach will generate a large number of atomic configurations representative of the ab initio liquid.
A subset of the generated liquid configurations will be selected to train an EAM potential.
Training the EAM potential on the selected configurations can improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
The proposed approach can reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
TOR-TILD uses EAM references as the baseline.
The target material regime comprises multicomponent high-entropy alloys in both solid and liquid states at or near their high melting temperatures.
The intervention is applicable to high-entropy alloys having five or more principal elements.
The intervention is applicable at temperatures near the alloy melting point.
Improved phase-space overlap and reduced integration-path mismatch will improve prediction of thermodynamic properties.
The effectiveness of the proposed approach depends on the quality of its training data.
The effectiveness of the proposed approach depends on the choice of machine-learning hyperparameters.
The proposed benchmark compares thermodynamic properties from the machine-learning-trained EAM potential against those from TOR-TILD's EAM references.
Free energy and entropy are proposed as benchmark measurements.
Failure to improve thermodynamic-property predictions relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references would falsify the hypothesis.
